newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian lev closes weaker at 507-510 per dlr.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian lev closes weaker at 507-510 per dlr.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev eased to 507-510 per dollar in very light interbank volume at Monday's close from 502-505 at the opening in anticipation of a further fall next month, dealers said.

"Several banks were buying foreign currency before noon, building up forex positions in anticipation of a fresh lev fall in January following comments by the central bank governor," a commercial bank dealer said.
Trade ended early ahead of the New Year holiday, dealers said. Markets will be closed in Bulgaria from December 31 through January 2.

Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) governor Lyubomir Filipov said on Sunday that the lev was likely to weaken further next month because foreign debt payments would be a priority for the BNB and it could provide only a limited support for the lev due to its low currency reserves.
Bulgaria has to pay some $150 million coupon on its Brady bonds on January 28.
BNB foreign currency reserves stood at $525 million at the end of November, down from $1,408 million a year earlier. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569; 981 4145
